patch.value: Declared read-intent token budgets are written to a flag three of five intent commands do not accept, so the shipped intent layer overruns its own declaration by up to 43.8x

Every built-in read intent shipped on 2026-07-30 declares a token_budget, and applyContextIntentProjection writes that budget into projected.tokenBudget at src/sdk/context-intent-contracts.ts line 323 for all five intent commands. Only next and context actually declare a --token-budget flag: list, get and search reject it as an unknown option, so the declared budget is written into a key those commands never read and is silently discarded. Measured on the live 2201-item tracker: list --for triage returns 315,037 bytes (about 78.8k tokens) against a declared 1,800 (43.8x); get --for inspect returns 252,575 bytes (about 63.1k tokens) against 3,200 (19.7x); search --for discover 17,662 bytes against 1,800 (2.45x); next --for execute 5,123 bytes against 1,200 (1.07x). The single conforming pair is the only one whose command accepts the flag, which is the natural control that proves the mechanism. The response envelope carries no budget, estimated_tokens or degradation field at all, so a consumer cannot detect the overrun from the payload. The list intent narrows fields correctly (projection.mode fields, 16 named fields) and applies no row bound, so all 306 open items are emitted with truncated false and has_more false.

Every declared intent budget is enforced at one response egress point rather than by a per-command flag, so no intent can overrun its own declaration; list, get and search either declare --token-budget or the intent layer refuses to claim a budget it cannot apply, with no silent third option; the response envelope of every intent-projected read carries the resolved budget, the measured estimate and the degradation actually applied, so a consumer can detect an overrun without measuring bytes itself; a negative-control test asserts that an intent whose command lacks budget enforcement fails the build rather than shipping; the published evidence table records observed versus declared tokens per intent on a corpus of at least the current tracker size
Make a declared intent budget an enforced ceiling instead of an advisory number
Agents get the bounded payload the intent promises rather than a 20x to 44x surprise that silently consumes the window
Every intent-projected read on a real corpus is currently unbounded, so the token-efficiency guarantee the intent layer was built to deliver does not hold on any command except next
The intent layer shipped 2026-07-30 and its budget declaration is inert on three of five commands from the first release, before any consumer depends on it

author: harness:claude-code
message: Budget enforcement cannot honestly close while three of five declared budgets are below the smallest projection their command can emit

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Conformance re-measure 2026-07-30 (evening), at HEAD after the context-budget bundle merged at 14:33Z. Enforcement shipped and works. The three intents this item measured as 43.8x, 19.7x and 2.45x over their declared budgets are now inside them: list triage 1,045 of 1,800 tokens in 6,250 bytes, get inspect 1,208 of 3,200 in 6,565 bytes, search discover 1,300 of 1,800 in 7,219 bytes. The receipt now carries the resolved budget, the measured estimate and the applied degradation, which closes the envelope half of the acceptance criteria.

Two of this item's own criteria are still open, and one of them is now falsified rather than merely unmet.

The criterion that list, get and search either declare the budget flag or the intent layer refuses to claim a budget it cannot apply, with no silent third option, is falsified. All three still exit 2 with unknown_option on --token-budget. All three nevertheless claim a budget in the receipt and enforce it at egress. That is precisely the silent third option the criterion forbids: the budget is claimed and applied on a command that offers no way to adjust it. It is reachable today, not latent. pm list --limit 200 --for triage returns budget_receipt_only with zero rows, and pm get <id> --depth deep --for inspect does the same, and neither has any override.

The criterion that a negative control asserts an intent whose command lacks budget enforcement fails the build is still unmet, and the day showed the control was pointed at the wrong invariant. Enforcement presence was never the fragile part. Reachability of the declared number is, and that is now tracked separately as a blocking dependency on this item, since enforcement cannot honestly be called complete while three of five declared ceilings cannot be met by the commands that declare them.

Method note for whoever picks this up: measure with the flag on the two commands that accept it. The floor is only visible by raising the ceiling until rows appear. next execute yields nothing at 1200, nothing at 2000, and 1,438 tokens of content at 4000. context orient yields nothing at 2400, nothing at 8000, and 8,417 tokens at 40000.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Re-measured 2026-08-01 at 2026.8.1. The falsified acceptance criterion recorded on 2026-07-30 is now satisfied on the list family: --token-budget is accepted on list, list-open, list-all, list-closed, get, search, next, context and deps, and is declared in each of their help outputs. It is rejected only when supplied without --for, and the refusal is correct and explains itself: "--token-budget requires a declared context intent selected with --for". The earlier reading that list, get and search exit 2 on the flag was taken without --for and is superseded by this measurement.

Conformance on the list family is now good rather than absent. On 330 open items: budget 1200 gives 12 rows, estimated_tokens 1145, budget_derived_limit 12; budget 3000 gives 38 rows, estimated_tokens 3190. Plain list --json for comparison is 74,457 bytes. The 43.8x divergence recorded for list:triage on 2026-07-30 is gone, and no result is omitted.

Two residuals, both routed rather than re-filed here. The budget stops binding above the default page cap and the derived-limit field is omitted exactly when the clamp applies; that is the new ceiling item. The emitted payload divided by four exceeds estimated_tokens by roughly seven percent at every budget measured, in the same direction; that belongs to the accounting item.
